issues.description: The package supplies code, documentation, and a firm identifier list, not a prepared analysis panel. Local one-row probes establish readable Datastream and Worldscope candidates, but exact author-table mappings and required history remain unverified; the regulated-firm, GDP, FactSet, and RavenPack inputs also lack compatible verified routes.

The SAS source includes two external macro files through an unresolved path macro and later calls `array` and `do_over`. The work-item inventory lists no `Do_over.sas` or `array.sas`; their definitions and paths must be supplied to close this stage.

The Worldscope macro obtains a table name and frequency from `wsitem`, then joins `qa.ws&dataset.data` on item and keys. The package does not identify those resolved source tables or show that a local wide `WRDS_WS_FUNDA` table reproduces the required long-form joins for all ten item numbers.

The entry scripts retain literal `Insert file path` placeholders in their global roots. Actual shared SAS and Stata data, work, output, and helper-program paths must be configured before the author workflow can resolve its file handoffs.

Six SAS PROC EXPORT statements write `.dta`-named handoffs without an explicit DBMS identifier, while later SAS imports specify DTA and Stata consumes the same files. SAS documentation identifies DBMS as the output-type selector and lists DTA for Stata `.dta` files; making that format explicit is a supported interoperability preparation.

Stage 4 line 72 specifies `replace` on a Stata `use` command, while the official current use manual lists `clear` and `nolabel`; nearby source context uses `clear` when loading the same intermediate. Propose replacing only this option, preserving the file and all downstream data and sample definitions. This is a documentation-supported preparation correction, not a claim based on a runtime failure or a Stata 18 syntax trial.

evidence.description: README stage 1 inputs, outputs, and purpose.
evidence.quote:
Step 1: 1_3_capital market data.sas (first part of codebase)
Input: Datastream, Worldscope (QA direct)
Output: quarterly_dataset, exchange_ids, annual_report_all_events
This code is used to combine capital market data into one table that can be used for our main analyses. We
also create separate datasets containing all information event dates and exchange information.

evidence.description: README stage 2 inputs and outputs.
evidence.quote:
Step 2: 2_Compile_1.do
Input: quarterly_dataset, exchange_ids, annual_report_all_events, regulatedfirms, GDP_Data
Output: quarterly_dataset_processed, quarterly_dataset_processed_identifiers, analysis_sample,
analysis_sample_identifiers, analysis_sample_annual_events
This do-file takes capital market data, data on regulated firms (Christensen et al., 2016), and GDP data to
construct the year-quarter data for our analysis. In the public code and files, we replace specific regulation
implementation dates with the first day of the quarter (yielding equivalent results in our analysis), and all
regulated firms in the final dataset are listed in identifiers.txt.

evidence.description: README stage 3 consumes stage 2 outputs and creates return/event intermediates.
evidence.quote:
Step 3: 1_3_capital market data.sas (second part of codebase)
Input: quarterly_dataset_processed, analysis_sample_annual_events, Datastream
Output: weekly_returns_processed, annual_events_1, annual_events_2
This code creates a dataset with weekly returns to be used for synchronicity calculations. In the second part
of this step, we create a sample with peer and focal firm returns around peer firm information events.

evidence.description: SAS identifier preparation independently reads security-master and security-map tables for Datastream and Worldscope.
evidence.quote:
proc sql;create table secmaster_1 as select seccode,id,typ,sedol,sedol2,cusip,isin,name,country
	from 	(select seccode,id,1 as typ,sedol,prevSedol,sedol2,prevSedol2,cusip,prevcusip,isin,name,country 
				from Qa.secmstrx where type_ = 1 
			 union all 
			 select seccode,id,6 as typ,sedol,prevSedol,sedol2,prevSedol2,cusip,prevcusip,isin,name,country 
				from qa.gsecmstrx where type_ = 10);
proc sql; create table secmaster_2 as select distinct a.*, b.vencode as Infocode, b.rank as DS_rank, d.vencode as Code, d.rank as WS_rank 
	from secmaster_1 a
	left join (select *, 1 as typ from qa.secmapx union select *, 6 as typ from qa.gsecmapx) b on a.seccode = b.seccode and a.typ=b.typ and b.ventype = 33
	left join (select *, 1 as typ from qa.secmapx union select *, 6 as typ from qa.gsecmapx) d on a.seccode = d.seccode and a.typ=d.typ and d.ventype = 10;

evidence.description: The initial SAS section creates the WORK DS_overview_pricing table consumed by the later SAS section.
evidence.quote:
proc sql; create table DS_overview_pricing as select distinct a.InfoCode, a.DsCode, a.adjtype, a.mdate, intnx('qtr',mdate,0,'b') as yearqtr format=yyqs8., 
		a.yearmonth, case when weekday(mdate) in(1,2,3) then intnx('week',mdate,-1,'b')+3 else intnx('week',mdate,0,'b')+3 end as week format ddmmyy9.,
		a.ExchIntCode, a.ExchCtryCode, a.isPrimExchQt, bid, ask, Currency, price, ret, ri, Volume, a.numshrs,
		price/(coalesce(e.midrate,1)) as Price_EUR, price/(coalesce(USD.midrate,1)) as Price_USD, 		
		a.spread, abs(price)*volume as volumevalue,
		volume*(abs(price)/coalesce(e.midrate,1)) as volumevalue_eur, volume*(abs(price)/coalesce(USD.midrate,1)) as volumevalue_USD,
		numshrs*abs(price)/(coalesce(e.midrate,1)) as MV_EUR, numshrs*abs(price)/(coalesce(USD.midrate,1)) as MV_USD, 
		coalesce(e.midrate,1) as FX, a.share_turnover
	from DS_overview_pricing a
	left join fx_EUR e on a.mdate=e.exratedate & a.currency=e.fromcurrcode
	left join fx_USD USD on a.mdate=USD.exratedate & a.currency=USD.fromcurrcode
;
proc datasets library=work NOLIST; delete del1 - del5; quit;
/*Cleaning Steps and final merge*/
proc sql; create table del as select distinct mdate, yearqtr, exchintcode, count(mdate) as stocks_per_day
	from DS_overview_pricing

		count(a.ret) as count, mean(MV_USD) as MV_USD
	from ds_overview_pricing a

Public verification was limited to official static World Bank and SAS documentation; no data payloads were requested and no page links were followed. Literal quotes remain below 25 words per URL.
